newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude prices rise, but diffs idle.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude prices rise, but diffs idle.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices rose, tracking the recovery of West Texas Intermediate (WTI), while the market for Alaskan crude stayed idle.
Outright prices for Alaska North Slope (ANS) rose 30 cents with WTI to $22.15/22.45 a barrel, with diffs at less $2.30.
Traders said a cargo of Alberta Koch crude was sold to a California broker for resale to a refinery. The 500,000 is due to load at Vancouver in mid-November, the seller said earlier.
A refiner on Friday sold a 500 barrel-per-day parcel of San Joaquin Valley heavy crude oil at postings.
The seller said they were long crude, but the sale was not caused by delays in running a crude train from the Valley to Los Angeles, slated to begin November 1.
Buyers bid at $2.50 under November WTI but favored greater discounts because of poor margins. Meanwhile, a major producer kept his offer at $2.10.
Line 63 diffs remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for November delivery.
Kern River, from California's San Joaquin Valley, held at $17.20/17.40 a barrel, after rising with a postings change October 8.
Prices for Long Beach-based Wilmington crude also remained stagnant at $18.60/18.70 a barrel.
